annotation.title_clean: Awareness and Development of Industry 4.0: Case of Latvia
annotation.title_en: Awareness and Development of Industry 4.0: Case of Latvia
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Petrovica, S.; Strautmane, M.; Anohina-Naumeca, A.
annotation.venue: Baltic DB&IS 2022 Doctoral Consortium and Forum (CEUR Workshop Proceedings, Vol-3158)
annotation.summary_en: Desk research on Latvia's awareness and development of Industry 4.0, covering digitalization indicators, national strategic and policy documents, educational events, research projects, higher-education integration, and required skills. Robotics appears only as one Industry 4.0 pillar; the paper contains no robot governance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Latvia ranks below the EU average in digital skills (43% with basic skills versus 56% EU average).
Only 42% of Latvian SMEs have at least basic digital technology integration, versus 60% in the EU.
National strategic and policy documents support Industry 4.0 but awareness and education need strengthening.
Around 14% of jobs may disappear and 32% change significantly due to automation.
Skills in data, AI, automation, robotics and soft skills should be purposefully developed.
